rejected.what: a save interval fine enough to resolve the thermal regime
rejected.reason: the MSD has THREE regimes and this plan resolves two of them. Below tau_1 = D_T/v0^2 the translational noise beats the propulsion and the slope returns to 1; seeing that needs a save interval a decade under tau_1, which at this record length is 4e9 stored coordinates against A5's ceiling of 1e9. The window is bounded here and not resolved, and the short-lag end is a second plan rather than a finer version of this one

rejected.what: the integration timestep at A1's ceiling
rejected.reason: A1 allows a step three decades coarser, because for a free active particle the only discretisation error is holding the orientation fixed across a step. A saved frame would then fall between steps, so the step follows the save interval instead

rejected.what: the record at A2's own floor of a hundred persistence times
rejected.reason: A2's floor and A4's window floor cannot both be met at that record: 3000 s of window in 10000 s of record is a ratio of 0.3 against A2's own ceiling of 0.1. Two axes that never see each other conflict, and S4 resolves it by lengthening the record rather than shortening the window

numbers.name: bead_diameter
numbers.note: the laboratory's tracer, measured by the operator on 2026-09-19. Provenance of D_T and of the sweep's centre, NOT a parameter of abp_free

numbers.name: temperature
numbers.note: the room's, read off a thermometer. In this configuration temperature is constitutive -- a parameter of the noise amplitude with no mechanism that could fail to realise it -- so citing it records why the value was chosen and is not evidence about the model

numbers.name: viscosity
numbers.note: pure water; the entry's validity runs 288 to 298 K and the temperature above is inside it

numbers.name: translational_diffusivity
numbers.note: held fixed across the whole grid. One significant figure because the worst input carries one

numbers.name: rotational_diffusivity
numbers.note: the sphere's own Stokes-Einstein-Debye value, 3*D_T/d^2. This revision sits ON the realisable centre rather than off it, so every number here describes one physical particle. Unit 1/s and not rad^2/s: the registry gives rad the dimension A, so rad^2/s cannot enter any formula check 17 can evaluate, and a radian is dimensionless

numbers.name: self_propulsion_speed
numbers.note: 2.97 um/s at one significant figure

numbers.name: persistence_time_expected
numbers.note: 1/((d-1)*D_R) is 1/D_R in two dimensions. Consistent with the rotational diffusivity above BY CONSTRUCTION, which revision 2 was not: it carried the sweep top for one and the sweep bottom for the other, and A1 failed check 17 on the mismatch

numbers.name: thermal_crossover_time
numbers.note: tau_1 = D_T/v0^2, the EARLY crossover where the thermal regime gives way to the ballistic one. The three-regime structure is the reason this number exists: the MSD starts at slope 1, not 2

numbers.name: persistence_length_expected
numbers.note: 289 um at one figure. It bounds nothing -- A3 abstains because a free particle is not coupled to its image -- and is recorded so that is visible

numbers.name: peclet_thermal
numbers.note: the collapse variable v0/sqrt((d-1)*D_R*D_T) at this operating point. 100 gives Lambda = 1e4, where the maximum log-log slope is 1.98 -- the ballistic regime is present and clean. At Pe_thermal of 10 the maximum is 1.79 and at 1 it is 1.12

numbers.name: n_particles
numbers.note: non-interacting walkers, a statistics knob and not a density. A hundred keeps the trajectory inside two gigabytes at the save interval this point needs

numbers.name: integration_timestep_max
numbers.note: upper bound only. The free model has no length scale, so no displacement per step is constrained; the orientation held fixed over one step is the only error the integrator makes, and D_R*dt is the only group it can depend on

numbers.name: total_simulated_time_min
numbers.note: floor only; A5 bounds the run from above

numbers.name: lag_to_record_ratio_max
numbers.note: the largest share of the record one lag may span

numbers.name: save_interval_max
numbers.note: upper bound. The crossover and the short-time slope live below tau_p, and a save interval near tau_p would record only the diffusive tail

numbers.name: fit_lag_range_lower_bound_min
numbers.note: the window parameter of effective_translational_diffusivity; a value read earlier is D_T under that name (contracts/observables.json)

numbers.name: max_lag_time_min
numbers.note: the window parameter of mean_squared_displacement, bounded from BELOW here: opposite to tracer_diffusivity, whose window is bounded from above to stay free

numbers.name: total_simulated_time_point
numbers.note: four hundred persistence times. NOT A2's floor, which is a hundred: A4 requires a window of at least 3000 s and A2 requires the window to be at most a tenth of the record, so the pair forces at least 30000 s and 400 tau_R is the next round multiple above it. The 400 is a decision and carries no grade; the seconds inherit E4 from the persistence time

numbers.name: save_interval_point
numbers.note: the save interval is set AT the early crossover tau_1 = D_T/v0^2, four decades below A4's 1 s ceiling. That resolves the whole ballistic window and puts the shortest lag at the thermal boundary rather than inside it: the regime below tau_1 is bounded by this plan and not resolved by it, which is recorded as a rejection rather than left to be discovered

numbers.name: integration_timestep_point
numbers.note: a decade below the save interval so a saved frame never falls between steps. Three decades under A1's ceiling, which for this configuration is D_R*dt <= 0.01 and nothing else -- there is no length in the free model for a displacement-per-step bound to compare against

numbers.name: box_length_point
numbers.note: NOT A BOUND AND THE CARD SAYS SO. A3 abstains because nothing couples a free particle to its periodic image, so no axis constrains the box; the engine needs one and this is it. Ten persistence lengths keeps the wrapping sparse for a reader looking at raw coordinates, and the estimator reads unwrapped positions regardless

numbers.name: max_lag_time_point
numbers.note: at A4's floor, thirty persistence times. Taking more window would push the record longer still through A2's ratio without buying a regime the run does not already cover

numbers.name: lag_to_record_ratio
numbers.note: the window as a share of the record, under A2's 0.1. This is the number that made the record four times A2's floor rather than equal to it. 3000/40000 is 0.075 and one significant figure is 0.08, which is what explore mode allows a value whose inputs carry one figure each -- writing 0.075 claimed a precision neither input has

assumptions.statement: The thermal Peclet number is set to 100 at this single operating point, where Lambda = 1e4 and the maximum log-log slope is 1.98. Chosen so the ballistic regime is present rather than marginal: at Pe_thermal of 10 the maximum slope is 1.79 and at 1 it is 1.12.
assumptions.falsifier: a run whose maximum log-log slope falls below 1.9, which would mean this point does not reach the regime it was chosen to reach

assumptions.statement: A thousand non-interacting walkers per point. Nothing physical picks this; it is the statistics knob, and the particles do not interact so it is not a density.
assumptions.falsifier: a statistical error on D_eff that this ensemble cannot reach inside budget

assumptions.statement: A lag may span at most a tenth of the record so that every lag in the fit is determined by many displacements rather than by one.
assumptions.falsifier: a weighted fit whose slope is unchanged when the longest lag is shortened retires this fraction

kb_refs.claim: The particles in the bottle in use have a diameter of 5 micrometres, with a coefficient of variation no greater than 2 per cent, measured directly by the operator on 2026-09-19.
The laboratory's ambient temperature is 20 degrees Celsius, read off a thermometer by the operator. It is a reading and not a setpoint, and it is the room's rather than the sample's.
Dynamic viscosity of pure water near 293 K is of order one millipascal second, and it changes by roughly two percent per kelvin in that neighbourhood.
